text:
Alejandro: Pushed a profiling pass across A10/T4/L4/A100/H100 focused on continuous-batching behavior + kernel fit. saw some surprising tail regressions when batch token budgets grew beyond a device-specific point. digging in and proposing threshold tweaks.

Maya: Can you drop the 99p tail numbers? quick summary pls.

Alejandro: 99p latencies (p50/p95/p99) summary: A100 9/32/210 ms, H100 8/28/170 ms, A10 12/48/420 ms, L4 18/75/860 ms, T4 22/110/1200 ms. these are under mixed-size realtime traffic with KV cache enabled and prefix reuse ~18%.

Cheng: ouch T4 and L4 look painful. any sign it's kernel-selector thrashing or KV fragmentation?

Alejandro: both. kernel selector keeps flipping between small-seq and long-seq kernels when large batches include a few long-context requests. that flip forces extra copies / kernel relaunch that kills tail. KV cache fragmentation adds extra memcpy overhead for mixes with many warmed but partially-compatible caches.

Alejandro: pasted a quick sampling from the profiler:

```
# perf-sample
device: T4
batch_tokens: 42k
active_kernels: [small_seq, long_seq]
kernel_switches: 6
memcpy_ms: 34
compute_ms: 88
cpu-sched-wait_ms: 12
observed_tail_ms: 1120
```

Maya: thanks. so proposal is to cap max tokens-per-batch per GPU to avoid kernel-switch churn?

Alejandro: yes. pragmatic thresholds that trade a tiny throughput loss for big tail win. early numbers: H100=120k, A100=80k, A10=48k, L4=24k, T4=18k (tokens-per-batch). also add a second-level queue policy to prioritize homogeneous-length packing: prefer mixing similar sequence-lengths into the same micro-batch.

Cheng: i like the homogeneous pack idea. what's the plan to implement without causing starvation for long requests? we can't block large-context customer requests.

Alejandro: plan: 1) soft cap per device (reject exceeding tokens with fallback to lower-cap model or async enqueue), 2) packer preference window of 200ms to attempt homogeneous grouping, 3) fallback path: if a request waits > 250ms, force dispatch even if mixed.

Sam: rollout plan? canary all changes on a single rack/zone first?

Alejandro: yes. canary on eu-west-1 H100 pool + one T4 rack for worst-case. telemetry hooks added to the console: per-route token-distribution, kernel-switch rate, memcpy overhead. if p99 improves >20% and throughput loss <3% we roll.

Lina: i'll add dashboard tiles and an eval job to the perf harness. can you add the synthetic workload config you used? I want to replicate the skew and prefix-reuse ratio.

Alejandro: pasted the synth load here:

```
# synth-workload: mixed-real-time
traffic mix: 60% short (<=128), 30% medium (129-1024), 10% long (>1024)
kv-prefix-reuse: 18%
burst pattern: poisson lambda=8rps per connection, 50ms jitter
test duration: 30m
```

Lina: got it, i'll schedule a run tonight and wire perf-bot alerts to the thread.

perf-bot: ALERT: deployment 2026-03-17/09:22 - kernel-switch-rate spike detected on T4 pool (x1.9) correlated with increased 99p latency. Suggested actions: reduce max_tokens_per_batch for T4 by 25% and enable homogeneous_packing window.

Cheng: quick thought — kernel-selector could benefit from a hysteresis window to avoid flip-flopping when avg seq length hops around threshold. add a 10% hysteresis on sequence-length thresholds.

Alejandro: good call. will add hysteresis to selector: require sustained median shift for 5 consecutive batches before switching kernels.

Maya: who owns the canary rollout tickets?

Sam: i'll create the canary/rollout ticket and assign to Alejandro + Cheng. include metrics and automatic rollback if p99 regresses >10% or throughput drops >6%.

Alejandro: thanks. next steps: update runtime config PR with device caps + homogenous_packer + selector hysteresis; Lina will add dashboards + perf harness job; Sam will open canary ticket; Cheng to pair on selector hysteresis impl. aiming for canary tomorrow morning.

Maya: :thumbsup: keep the change small and observable.

Alejandro: uploading config snippet to the PR in a sec.```
